conclusions: All five Stage C sites are op=index (locate/read an existing index root), pathId=P1, symbol=resolveAgentWorkspaceDir; they are NOT asset-creation flows and are NOT circular (unlike Stage B S26).

None of the five sites has a trusted request-level identity at the call site: they run with cfg+agentId only (background gateway startup loop, config-time resolveMemoryBackendConfig, cache-factory MemoryIndexManager.get, and the CogniWeave/Qmd manager constructors).

The canonical Resource Resolver resolveMemoryWorkspaceHandle requires tenantId + userId + server-trusted actor + ownership-bound agentAssetId + Catalog; those inputs are not available at these sites as they stand today.

A cfg-only resolver swap would be a fake retirement and is forbidden by the Stage C mandate; therefore this slice does NOT switch the five production call sites (the shadow module item7-w5-index-last.ts also decides keep-legacy-index).

The honest remediation is threading server-trusted call-entry identity to these sites with an explicit personal_local compat path vs managed_enterprise fail-closed split; that threading spans callers outside Stage C's fixed file set and must be accepted independently before any production switch.

This slice ships the controlled narrow interface resolveMemoryIndexWorkspaceHandle (authorize + restricted handle only; no dir creation, no Catalog write) plus full per-site and aggregate fail-closed tests, and a Semantic Gate CR.
The accepted baseline stays 12 and is NOT decremented; canonicalCountClaimed=false and canonicalLedgerUpdated=false; the retirement scan is untouched.
S25's accepted (landed) status is not rolled back; Stage B (S01/S02/S26/S27) remains blocked and is not processed here.

contract: Accept a server-resolved security profile (resolveSecurityProfile; never client RPC input).
personal_local: return an explicit security-profile-gated legacy compat locator; never used as a managed fallback.
managed_enterprise: require server-trusted tenantId + userId + actor; agentId slug is not ownership proof.
Resolve only an EXISTING canonical/active binding via the canonical resolver (resolveMemoryWorkspaceHandle), injected as a port.
Fail closed on catalog miss, ambiguity, cross-tenant, grant/ownership mismatch, missing membership SoT, stale fencing token.
Bind the index namespace to tenantId + resourceId so same-named agents never share an index root across tenants.
Halt (do not start/continue) when workspace lifecycle is retired/purged/moving/recovery_required.
Never create directories, never write the Catalog, never enable schema v2 or LIVE, never fall back to a host path.
On any denial: return without scanning/reading/writing an index (guardedMemoryIndexStart proves zero side effects).
